title: ChatHEA assistant guides high-entropy alloy catalysts for fuel cells
summary: ChatHEA, a domain-specific LLM assistant for high-entropy alloy electrocatalysis, guided synthesis and screening of 100 five-element alloy catalysts. The FeCoCuPtIr catalyst reached a peak power density of 0.789 W cm-2 in a fuel cell and outperformed commercial Pt/C in electrochemical tests. These figures are reported by the institutional press release; its numeric activity values and DOE target are not given. The catalog date is the paper's 14 March 2026 publication date, stated in the 8 July press release; the full paper was not reviewed.
organization: Tohoku University, Advanced Institute for Materials Research (AIMR)

evidence.tested: 100 five-element alloy catalysts were screened by high-throughput experimentation; FeCoCuPtIr outperformed commercial Pt/C in electrochemical tests and reached 0.789 W cm-2 peak power density in a fuel cell.
evidence.unknown: Not reported; the page gives no detailed durability data and lists no limitations.
evidence.ai_role: ChatHEA, a domain-specific LLM assistant, supported literature review, element design, experiment planning, data processing and activity analysis.
